HELP.INTRO: Quick explanations of how the manager connects panels, plugins, MQTT, and updates.
HELP.PANELS_BODY: A panel is the manager's logical device record. Assign its discovered MAC address to keep that record attached to the physical display even if the display's network name changes. Groups let you send shared night mode and brightness settings.
HELP.PLUGINS_BODY: A plugin profile describes an integration and its behavior. An instance connects one profile to a real device and supplies its variables. Panel bindings decide which instance is shown on a favorite, tile, or hardware button.
HELP.ROUTES_BODY: Routes forward messages between external topics and panel topics. A payload filter can match text or compare a JSON path such as buttons.b1 against a value. Templates can change the outgoing payload.
HELP.BACKUPS_BODY: Scheduled and manual backups contain the manager configuration and database. Keep the credential-encryption key from secrets/manager_encryption_key in a separate safe backup; a data archive alone cannot decrypt broker credentials.
HELP.HEALTH_BODY: Subscribe to the topic below to build notifications in your own automation system. Each event is a JSON object with a stable event name, severity, timestamp, panel identity, and event-specific details. Turn off health notifications on a panel to suppress its events.
HELP.HEALTH_EVENTS: Events: panel.offline, panel.online, panel.unexpected_reboot, panel.low_memory, and panel.memory_recovered.
HELP.UPDATES_BODY: Firmware packages include their version manifest. HMI uploads can declare which panel firmware profiles they support. A staged HMI rollout updates a canary first and starts one queued panel only after the previous panel reports the requested HMI hash.
HELP.PANEL_CONTEXT_BODY: Add the logical panel, then assign its discovered MAC address. Health events are also published to nspanelmanager/event/health; disable notifications per panel if it should be excluded.
HELP.PLUGINS_CONTEXT_BODY: Use Plugins to define reusable integrations and Instances to configure each real device. Required instance variables are listed when you create or edit an instance.
HELP.ROUTES_CONTEXT_BODY: External-to-panel routes send external state to a panel command topic. Panel-to-external routes forward panel events. JSON equality filters support dotted paths such as buttons.b1 and match the value exactly.
HELP.BACKUPS_CONTEXT_BODY: Download backups regularly and store them outside this manager. Back up the credential-encryption key separately and keep it available when restoring the database.
HELP.UPDATES_CONTEXT_BODY: Confirm the uploaded HMI profile matches the panel before sending it. For several panels, select a canary and targets; the next target starts only after the canary reports success.

HMI.TITLE: Panel updates
HMI.DESCRIPTION: Manage panel firmware and display updates.
HMI.UPLOAD_FIRMWARE_DESCRIPTION: Upload the versioned package produced by pnpm firmware:compile. It contains the ESPHome OTA image and a manifest, so the manager reads the compiled version automatically. The standalone .bin is still available for other workflows.
HMI.ROLLOUT_DESCRIPTION: Manually update one panel as the canary. After it reports the new version and maintains continuous uptime for the stability window, opted-in unified panels update one at a time. If you already installed the uploaded version before enabling rollout, stage it from that panel without reflashing.
HMI.ENABLE_ROLLOUT_HELP: Panels marked below can be updated after the canary passes.
HMI.CANCEL_ROLLOUT_HELP: Cancel stops queued panels. An update already sent to a panel will finish.
HMI.CONFIRM_DELETE_FIRMWARE: Delete firmware {{version}} from the manager? This removes the uploaded image and invalidates its download links. It does not change firmware already installed on panels.
HMI.PUSH_FIRMWARE_DESCRIPTION: Manually update the canary panel here. The panel downloads the binary from this manager and verifies it with MD5 before flashing.
HMI.FORCE_UPDATE_HELP: Start downloading immediately without waiting for confirmation on the panel.
HMI.OPTED_IN_HELP: Opted-in panels update after the canary passes.
HMI.ROLLOUT_REQUIRES_UNIFIED: Automatic rollout requires detected unified firmware.
HMI.ADD_PANEL_BEFORE_FIRMWARE: Add a panel under Panels before requesting a firmware update.
HMI.NO_FIRMWARE_HELP: Upload the versioned ESPHome OTA .zip package to push firmware from the manager.
HMI.UPLOAD_HMI_DESCRIPTION: The latest upload becomes the selected version. Files still referenced by active panel links are retained until those links expire. Its SHA-256 checksum is the HMI version ID reported by updated panels.
HMI.COMPATIBILITY_HELP: Select only profiles that use this HMI layout. The manager blocks updates to panels with an incompatible profile.
HMI.HMI_ROLLOUT_HELP: Choose one canary and one or more targets. The manager waits for a successful HMI version report before starting each next panel.
HMI.INCOMPATIBLE_PROFILE: Not compatible with this HMI file
HMI.CHOOSE_PANEL_HELP: Send an update prompt, or force the panel to start downloading immediately.
HMI.FORCE_HMI_HELP: Start immediately without waiting for confirmation on the panel.
HMI.ADD_PANEL_BEFORE_HMI: Add a panel under Panels before requesting an HMI update.
HMI.NO_HMI_HELP: Choose a compatible Nextion .tft file above. It will be stored in the manager's persistent data directory.
HMI.BEFORE_UPDATE_HELP: Panels need manager HTTP OTA support from the current NSPanel firmware. Unified firmware uses an MQTT topic derived from the assigned device MAC. Set APP_PUBLIC_URL or HMI_PUBLIC_URL to an address reachable from the panel network. Firmware and HMI download links are valid for six hours.

BROKER.TITLE: MQTT broker
BROKER.DESCRIPTION: Connect the manager to the broker used by your NSPanel firmware and smart devices.
BROKER.URL_HELP: Use mqtt:// or mqtts:// with an optional port.
BROKER.PASSWORD_KEEP: Saved — leave blank to keep it
BROKER.NOTICE_SAVED: Broker settings saved. The manager will reconnect automatically.
BROKER.HTTP_LOG_DESCRIPTION: Optionally forward structured manager log records to an HTTP endpoint. Secrets are encrypted in the manager database and never returned to the browser.
BROKER.HTTP_LOG_ENABLE: Forward manager logs to an HTTP endpoint
BROKER.HTTP_LOG_URL_HELP: The manager sends HTTP POST requests with JSON records. The endpoint should respond with HTTP 200.
BROKER.HTTP_LOG_SECRET_KEEP: Saved — leave blank to keep it
BROKER.HTTP_LOG_TOKEN_SAVED: A bearer token is saved. It is not shown here.
BROKER.HTTP_LOG_PASSWORD_SAVED: A password is saved. It is not shown here.

ROUTES.TITLE: MQTT routes
ROUTES.DESCRIPTION: Connect incoming device states with panel commands, and panel actions with device commands.
ROUTES.EXTERNAL_EXAMPLE: For example, thermostat state to a panel display topic.
ROUTES.PANEL_EXAMPLE: For example, panel button event to a device command.
ROUTES.EMPTY_DESCRIPTION: Create a route below to connect your devices.
ROUTES.FORM_HELP: Source topics accept + and # wildcards. Optional payload filters can match text, the full payload, or a JSON value. Payload template tokens include payload, topic, nodeName, and JSON paths like json.temperature.
ROUTES.NAME: Route name
ROUTES.FILTER_CONTAINS_HELP: Matches this case-sensitive text anywhere in the payload.
ROUTES.JSON_PATH_HELP: Use dot-separated property names, such as buttons.b1.
ROUTES.TEMPLATE_HELP: For external-to-panel routes, the selected panel’s node name is used in the target topic.

USERS.TITLE: Local administrator accounts
USERS.DESCRIPTION: Local accounts control access. Optional SSO can sign in only to an existing account with the same verified email.
USERS.ADD_HELP: Use a unique email and a password with at least 12 characters.

LOGS.DESCRIPTION: Recent records from the manager's rotating log files. Log details may contain data written by configured scripts.
LOGS.ERROR_LOAD: Could not read the manager log files.
LOGS.EMPTY: No log entries match these filters.

BACKUPS.TITLE: Data backup
BACKUPS.DESCRIPTION: Download a ZIP containing the manager's complete persistent data folder.
BACKUPS.SCHEDULED_DESCRIPTION: Choose when the manager writes a ZIP and how many recent archives to keep.
BACKUPS.SCHEDULE_HELP: Five fields: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. Example:
BACKUPS.SCHEDULE_EXAMPLE_END: runs daily at 03:00 in the manager's timezone.
BACKUPS.FOLDER_HELP_END: Absolute paths work when the folder is writable and mounted persistently.
BACKUPS.RETENTION_HELP: Older scheduled ZIP files are deleted after a successful backup.
BACKUPS.ARCHIVE_PRIVACY: Archives are private ZIP files and are excluded from their own contents.
BACKUPS.DOWNLOAD_DESCRIPTION: The archive includes configuration, user accounts, saved script state, last-known device state, and files in the data folder such as logs. The ZIP is created for this download and is not stored on the server.
BACKUPS.HISTORY_DESCRIPTION: Restore the full manager configuration or one selected panel or plugin object. Restores are saved as new revisions.
BACKUPS.LOADING_SCOPES: Loading available panels and plugin objects…
BACKUPS.SCOPE_HELP_PANEL: Panel settings and plugin assignments are restored. The current panel name, MQTT node name, and physical device assignment are kept.
BACKUPS.SCOPE_HELP_PLUGIN-PROFILE: This profile may be shared. Restoring it changes the configuration used by every instance linked to it.
BACKUPS.SCOPE_HELP_PLUGIN-INSTANCE: Restores the instance name, enabled state, profile selection, and variables. The shared profile itself is unchanged.
BACKUPS.EMPTY_SCOPES: This revision has no panel or plugin objects that still exist in the current configuration.
BACKUPS.EMPTY_HISTORY: No configuration revisions have been recorded yet.
BACKUPS.SECURITY_TITLE: Keep the archive and secrets safe
BACKUPS.SECURITY_DESCRIPTION: The ZIP contains sensitive configuration and account data. Store it securely. The credential-encryption key and optional OIDC client secret are kept outside the data folder; back them up separately. Without the encryption key, saved MQTT credentials cannot be read.
BACKUPS.MANUAL_RESTORE_START: To restore, stop the manager, extract the archive contents into the configured
BACKUPS.MANUAL_RESTORE_END: , restore required deployment secrets separately, then start the manager again.
BACKUPS.CONFIRM_RESTORE: Restore the complete manager configuration from {{createdAt}}? This will create a new revision and reconnect the runtime.
BACKUPS.CONFIRM_SCOPED_RESTORE: Restore '{{name}}' from {{createdAt}}? This will create a new revision and reconnect the runtime.
BACKUPS.NOTICE_SCOPED_RESTORED: Selected configuration object restored and runtime reconnected.
BACKUPS.ERROR_LOAD_SCOPES: Could not load the objects available in this revision.
BACKUPS.ERROR_REFRESH_AFTER_RESTORE: Configuration was restored, but the page could not refresh. Reload to see the current settings.
BACKUPS.ERROR_RESTORE: Could not restore this configuration revision.
BACKUPS.ERROR_SCOPED_RESTORE: Could not restore this configuration object.
